level: private archive restore component; not product activation or production migration
componentAcceptance: restoreMigrationArchives verifies both private archives before effects, stages each domain, rechecks complete content, publishes into explicit fresh targets and preserves exact prior restores. Real schema 5 SQLite data restores with identical lossless exports, original Bot ownership and unknown values. Repeating the same operation and independently importing the same archive do not duplicate receipts. Exceptions after a domain and after ledger publication resume from durable records; conflicting old targets remain untouched. Six focused tests pass and the related migration combination is 101 tests / 100 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped.
productAcceptance: None yet. This supplies a verified private restore component for W06.3 and T48/T49, but is not wired into product activation and does not prove stopped writers, old-plugin compatibility or production rollback. Scores remain 0/20 work packages, 42/63 scenarios and M0 11/12. activationSupported, postActivationRollbackSupported and stopWriteProvable remain false.
implementation: Each domain is copied under the owner-only operation directory and compared against the archive inventory before rename. Existing directories are accepted only when their complete structure and bytes match; conflicts never overwrite old data.
The SQLite archive is staged, checked by a fresh lossless export and published only to an absent target. Existing databases must have exactly the same logical export.
Immutable request/step records bind targets and archive content. Resume tolerates already-written markers, validates their file identity and completes missing domains/ledger without duplicate writes.

Public results contain counts and conservative capability flags, not private paths or payloads. The component is not imported by the product entry, so the npm runtime closure is unchanged; its test is registered in npm test.
testRuns: Focused restore: 6 tests / 6 pass / 0 fail, including two independent imports, same-operation replay, two interruption boundaries, conflict preservation, archive tampering and invalid inputs.
Related migration/package suites: 101 tests / 100 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped (Linux-only orchestration writer case).
Complete root regression: phase one 1600/1596/0/4 plus phase two 387/303/0/84 = 1987 tests / 1899 pass / 0 fail / 88 skipped.
preservedFailures: Initial fixture omitted legacyFile and failed before restore; it was corrected. A request digest TypeError and a test call that accidentally reused the old operation directory were fixed without weakening identity checks. No failure is rewritten as a first-pass success.
Interruption tests in this component throw at deterministic boundaries. Real child-process exit injection remains separate work.
limitations: Only explicit fresh or exactly matching targets are supported; this is not in-place upgrade, configuration activation, latest-data rollback or OS/launcher stop proof.
Filesystem mode bits are restored on non-Windows, but cross-platform ACL/ownership restoration is not claimed.
No real user profile, model inference, production process, push or release was used.
